score.notes: A confident, symmetrical temple front with a clear base→middle→crown reading: a terracotta-and-white arcaded body, a dominant blue central dome flanked by stepped minaret-towers with gold finials, and a disciplined bay rhythm of recessed white windows framing a taller central portal. Proportion is deliberate — the stepped silhouette from outer towers inward to the dome feels intentional and balanced, though the flanking towers read slightly stubby against the dome's mass. Color is the strongest asset: a well-judged terracotta/white/cobalt scheme with turquoise diaper-work banding and gold accents forms a genuine dominant-supporting-accent harmony with Byzantine/Mughal character. Detail is where it falls short of 'rich' — the turquoise tile banding and dome scaling add texture, but the large white wall fields and window surrounds stay flat and repetitive; relief depth is shallow and the ornament is applied as color rather than carved articulation, leaving sizable flat fields. Fidelity is clear and characterful — it reads unmistakably as a grand temple/shrine with a legible central entrance and presence, distinctive rather than generic, but not quite an iconic, namable landmark. An easy improvement — deepening the relief and breaking up the plain white bays — keeps every dimension short of exceptional.
